Dated notes for the course. Read the newest date first. These are source notes, not lecture slides.

## Key to labels

- Source tiers: T1 = official primary document; T2 = official secondary source or reputable report; T3 = industry or think-tank projection.
- Status: OPEN = still waiting; the official document or evidence has not appeared. WATCH = an official step is dated or pending; check it each week. settled = confirmed by an official source, with no step pending.
- In the weekly tables, NEW = first reported that week and Updated = a tracked item moved that week. Weeks with no movement on an item are not listed; the status table below gives each item's latest position.
- Boxes marked 官方中英文本 or 原文 hold the verbatim official text. Each passage is quoted once, at its first appearance on the page; later mentions link the source.

## 6 Oct 2026: LegCo spectrum restatement, new Sandbox restricted flying zones {#week-2026-10-06}

- On 6 October the Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development told a Legislative Council (LegCo) panel that the drone spectrum licensing launched in October 2025 is aligned with Mainland spectrum planning and will help future cross-boundary drone operations. This restates existing policy; it is not a new spectrum instrument, and the 1430–1444 MHz licence is still limited to the Regulatory Sandbox.
- A Government Notice (G.N. 5936), dated 21 September and in effect from 26 September, designates restricted flying zones to support Regulatory Sandbox pilot projects. It was found after the week closed.
- Mainland: Xinhua reported on 30 September that the Ministry of Public Security has disclosed an administrative-penalty benchmark for drone offences, in force on issuance. The ministry’s own text has not been read.

## 4 Oct 2026: Transport secretary briefs LegCo; Action Plan still being drawn up {#week-2026-10-04}

- On 2 October the Secretary for Transport and Logistics briefed a Legislative Council (LegCo) panel on the First Five-Year Plan and the 2026 Policy Address. The Chinese-only press release restates earlier commitments; it is a briefing, not a new legal instrument.
- The Working Group will keep working on the Action Plan this year. Its full text is still not published.
- The briefing restated three points: >140 regularised projects (PA 2026 ¶137); drafting of a dedicated law for unconventional aircraft to be completed next year and sent to LegCo; and a smart low-altitude traffic management system from 2028.

### 27 Sep 2026: Transport secretary meets Mainland civil aviation regulator in Beijing {#week-2026-09-27}

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show the 27 Sep 2026 note"}

- On 23 September the Secretary for Transport and Logistics, with the Permanent Secretary and the Director-General of Civil Aviation, met Deputy Administrator Liang Nan of the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC) in Beijing.
- Hong Kong’s press release lists the low-altitude economy among the aviation topics discussed, next to First Five-Year Plan and Policy Address measures on connectivity, air cargo and sustainable aviation fuel. The CAAC’s own Chinese notice of the meeting does not mention 低空经济 in its body.
- This is policy coordination only: no new legal instrument, Sandbox result or market figure.

### 20 Sep 2026: Policy Address and First Five-Year Plan set low-altitude timelines {#week-2026-09-20}

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show the 20 Sep 2026 note"}

- On 16 September the Chief Executive’s 2026 Policy Address set the aim of making Hong Kong the Asia-Pacific hub for innovative low-altitude applications. The First Five-Year Plan (2026–2030), announced the same day, repeats that aim.
- The Policy Address says the government will formulate an Action Plan on Developing Low-Altitude Economy with three actions: cross-boundary logistics trial flights as early as possible, a smart low-altitude traffic management system from 2028, and drafting a law for unconventional aircraft over 150 kg. The plan’s text is not published.
- The Policy Address annex sets two Transport and Logistics Bureau dates: the traffic management system from 2028 (indicator 34) and drafting of the over-150 kg law complete within 2027 (indicator 35).

#### What this note added

### 13 Sep 2026: Transport secretary’s speech; Mainland air traffic draft closes for comment {#week-2026-09-13}

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show the 13 Sep 2026 note"}

- On 10 September the Secretary for Transport and Logistics gave a speech, issued as a government press release: >140 CAD application approvals since Jun 2025 (STL speech), a focus on Sandbox X, and a Hong Kong–Kazakhstan memorandum of understanding (MoU) on the low-altitude economy, exchanged on 9 September.
- The speech previewed the Policy Address and First Five-Year Plan for the following week; neither was published in this window.
- Mainland: comments on the Civil Aviation Administration of China’s draft air traffic management rules closed on 11 September. The page still shows a draft only.

#### What this note added

| Area | Status | Detail |
|------|--------|--------|
| STL GIA speech (HKUST forum) | **NEW (T1 speech)** | Regularisation under existing CAD guidelines; >140 CAD application approvals since Jun 2025 (STL speech); Sandbox X for cross-boundary / unconventional / passenger-carrying; HK–Kazakhstan MoU attested (exchange **2026-09-09**); PA / First Five-Year Plan previewed for week after 2026-09-10 — **not** published in this window |
| CAAC ATM Rules Ch.12 UAS | **Updated (clock; still draft)** | Comments closed **2026-09-11**; still 征求意见稿; **not** promulgated |

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="原文 · Chinese original"}
**CAAC ATM Rules Ch.12 UAS** — [「中国民用航空局修订了《民用航空空中交通管理规则》，形成《民用航空空中交通管理规则（征求意见稿）》，现向社会公开征求意见。」…「意见反馈截止时间为2026年9月11日。」]{lang="zh-Hans"} ([source](https://www.caac.gov.cn/HDJL/YJZJ/202608/t20260811_231462.html))

### 5 Sep 2026: First weekly note; Mainland air traffic draft adds a drone chapter {#week-2026-09-05}

:::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show the 5 Sep 2026 note"}

- First weekly note. Hong Kong had no new primary changes on the Action Plan, Sandbox X cross-boundary results, advisory circulars, spectrum, the Working Group or LegCo, Cap. 448G s.12(2)(c), or who issued the HK\$350bn figure.
- Mainland: on 11 August 2026 the Civil Aviation Administration of China published a consultation draft of its air traffic management rules (comments to 11 September), adding Chapter 12 on unmanned aircraft.
- The draft is not yet in force. It is not the dedicated airworthiness (Art. 34) or implementing (Art. 225) regulation under the Civil Aviation Law.

#### What this note added

| Area | Status | Detail |
|------|--------|--------|
| Civil Aviation Law Art.34/225 follow-ons | **Updated (not yet law)** | NEW CAAC ATM Rules **draft** with UAS Ch.12 (2026-08-11) — [CAAC](https://www.caac.gov.cn/HDJL/YJZJ/202608/t20260811_231462.html) |
